goal: Build a JSON toolkit as a Python package minijson/ without using the json module. minijson/parser.py: loads(text) -> Python value for the full JSON grammar: objects, arrays, strings with all escapes including \uXXXX and surrogate pairs, numbers (integers become int, anything with a fraction or exponent becomes float), true, false, null, and surrounding whitespace. Invalid input (trailing commas, single quotes, leading zeros like 01, unescaped control characters in strings, trailing garbage, empty input) raises minijson.JSONError (a ValueError subclass defined in minijson/__init__.py) whose message includes the 1-based line and column of the problem as 'line L column C'. minijson/writer.py: dumps(value, indent=None, sort_keys=False) -> str. Compact output uses ', ' and ': ' separators like the standard library default; with indent=N it nests with N spaces, ', ' becomes ',' at line ends, and empty containers print as [] and {}. Non-ASCII characters are escaped as \uXXXX (surrogate pairs above U+FFFF). Floats print with repr; nan and infinity raise ValueError; keys must be str or raise TypeError. minijson/pointer.py: resolve(doc, pointer) implements RFC 6901 JSON Pointer ('' is the whole doc, ~1 means / and ~0 means ~, array indices are decimal without leading zeros); a missing path raises KeyError. The package exposes loads, dumps, resolve and JSONError from minijson/__init__.py. Also: python -m minijson [--indent N] [--sort-keys] reads JSON on stdin and prints it reformatted; on JSONError it prints the message to stderr and exits 1. Include a pytest suite.
